Keahi Kawaha: Kawaha gives Alabama an elite field general who sees throwing windows before they open. He pairs advanced anticipation with pinpoint accuracy, allowing his receivers to catch the ball in stride and keep moving. That command of the passing game gives him the profile of a franchise quarterback.
Tyrice Matthews: Matthews brings elite arm strength and effortless velocity from the left side. The Washington quarterback can drive the ball deep without giving up placement, forcing a defense to account for throws other passers struggle to reach. His downfield accuracy gives an offense a rare foundation for explosive plays.
Darnell Jacobs: Jacobs gives Georgia a dominant right tackle who can take control of a block with the force of his first strike. At 317 pounds, he pairs overwhelming strength with powerful hands that keep defenders under control. Those traits give him the profile of a franchise tackle.
Kevin Matthews Jr: Matthews anticipates the throw and covers enough ground to turn a passing window into a takeaway chance. Colorado can trust his range over the deep middle and use his instincts to challenge throws to either side. His elite ball skills give him cornerstone potential in the secondary.
Kofi Chiamaka: Chiamaka gives Ohio State a 6-foot-4 receiver with elite vertical speed and exceptional ball tracking. He can get behind a defender or rise above him when the throw is contested. The ability to win both ways downfield gives him the upside of a featured professional receiver.
Tre'Darius Bryant: Bryant can dictate the release with physical press technique and turn smoothly to stay with the receiver downfield. His recovery speed helps him close the window when a route stretches the coverage. Alabama has a lockdown corner with the tools to take on demanding boundary assignments.
Isaiah Roach: Roach gets off the line with sudden releases and accelerates quickly enough to create separation before coverage settles. Texas can use that speed to attack behind a secondary or make room underneath for another target. His breakaway ability gives the offense a dangerous option on deep throws.
Jahlil Jones-Mosley: Jones-Mosley reads offensive looks quickly and brings the presence to get Alabama’s defense organized before the snap. His recognition helps him put himself in position early as a play develops. That blend of instincts and leadership gives him the tools to command the middle of a professional defense.
Dameon Smith: Smith gives Missouri a receiver with reliable hands and the body control to adjust when the throw changes his path. Once he has the ball, he can find a lane and create extra yardage. His creativity makes him a player an offense can feature on touches in space.
Antez Robertson: Robertson accelerates sharply into deep routes and builds enough speed to put a defender in chase mode. Miami can use his smooth downfield movement to stretch a secondary and create room elsewhere. His speed gives the offense a direct way to turn vertical throws into explosive gains.
